result:
Both decision changes are recorded and applied, and the full test suite passes (35 passed).

What I changed:

- **`config.py`** — the only place in the code where these values are defined: `MAX_ITEMS_PER_USER` is now `100` (was 50) and `RETENTION_DAYS` is now `30` (was 90). I checked `api.py`, `storage.py`, and `test_api.py`, and they all import from `config.py` rather than hardcoding the numbers, so no other code changes were needed. The tests are written against `MAX_ITEMS_PER_USER` symbolically, so the limit tests automatically exercise the new value of 100.
- **Decision record** — per the README, the authoritative decision record lives in session memory. I updated the item-tracker ground-rules memory to state the new values (100 items/user, 30-day retention), noting on each line that the change was made today, and updated the memory index summary to match.

One observation: `RETENTION_DAYS` is defined in config but nothing in the codebase enforces retention yet — the storage layer is append-only with no pruning. So the 30-day window is recorded as a decision but will need an enforcement mechanism (e.g., a compaction/expiry pass) whenever that feature gets built.
